why: One function decides what looks like a credential, in Go (cli/internal/model/redact.go) and Python (shared/culprit_model/redaction.py). Both are held to these cases: the exact text each must give back, and whether looks_like_credential is true.

Phase 37 part 1 widens it before any statement text is read (PERFORMANCE_PLAN.md, Phase 37, carried in from the Phase 35 close-out, F2): password=… outside a URL, Slack tokens, and user:pass@host with no scheme. A connection string or a password literal in a normalised statement is exactly what it must catch.

cases.why: user:pass@ in a URL, the host kept
a password in a URL's query
a private key, the whole block

-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY----- end
